why: The small shape at the bottom-right of each figure moves to the top-left in the next figure, gets bigger and is turned upside down (the pin's dot goes from top to bottom). So C must have B's slashed circle at top-left, upside down, so the slash becomes '/'. C's bottom-right must be D's Z upside down, which is option 5. Option 2 has the right circle but its Z is not flipped.
trick: When a shape jumps from one corner to the other, check whether it also flips; compare the pin or slash direction.
